candidate.change_summary: Synthesized the final operational trial design with the revised fire safety limits, detailed the multi-channel community outreach strategy, integrated the strict 14-day privacy guardrails, and refined the board's evaluation metrics to focus on real-world access equity rather than administrative convenience.
candidate.reconsidered_answer: This reconsidered operational framework outlines the parameters for the 10-week weekend exhibition trial, structured to balance predictable flow with genuine public accessibility. Under the fire marshal's revised safety occupancy limits, a firm 40% floor will be reserved exclusively for walk-in arrivals, utilizing anonymous paper ticketing to protect access for those without online connectivity or advance planning. When safe limits are reached, the museum will offer reliable same-day return times on-site or by phone rather than maintaining a physical queue. Advance reservations will be capped at household-sized quantities (with separate assisted booking paths for larger groups) and will have a 30-minute arrival window, after which unused slots return to the walk-in pool. Staggered promotion efforts will launch simultaneously via neighborhood organizations and tourism channels to maintain geographic balance. To address privacy, booking systems will delete name and contact details after 14 days, keeping this information strictly walled off from membership and donor databases. To prevent passive continuation or skewed interpretations of success, weekly outcomes will be published transparently. If walk-in turn-aways increase for two consecutive weekends, the walk-in allocation will immediately increase. The success of the trial will be measured on whether timed entry reduced access barriers—tracking immediate entry, offered return times, confirmations, released capacity, and abandoned visits—rather than on the volume of reservations or the visual orderliness of the galleries.
